731d6688df08f9282ab73dbd7679468013e79433.title: Compatibility of released laws
731d6688df08f9282ab73dbd7679468013e79433.body:
Suppose \cref{obj:ass:overlap} holds. Let \(H\) be a probability law on the score interval \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), let \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_J\) be a measurable release rule, and let \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}\) be a probability law on \((R,A,Y)\). The compatible causal-law class \(\mathfrak M(H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\) of \cref{obj:def:compatible-law-class} is nonempty if and only if, for every \(r\in\mathcal R_J\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\mathrm{rel}}(R=r) &= H(C_r),\\
P_{\mathrm{rel}}(A=1,R=r) &= \int_{C_r} e\,H(de).
\end{aligned}
\]

1ccff2ef77bbb7b8e9d085b91ff3627ac14a6670.title: Bounds for optimal label ambiguity
1ccff2ef77bbb7b8e9d085b91ff3627ac14a6670.body:
Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap condition in \cref{obj:ass:overlap} holds for \(\varepsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Density floor.)} \(m_f>0\).
\item \textbf{(Label budget.)} \(K\geq 1\) is an integer.
\end{itemize}
Write \(\ell=1-2\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). For every \(H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:score-lower-density-class},
\[
\frac{m_f\ell^2}{2(1-\varepsilon)K}\leq\Delta_K(H).
\]
For every probability law \(H\) on \(\mathcal E\), the equal-width release \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_K\) given by
\[
g(e)=\min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac{K(e-\varepsilon)}{\ell}\right\rfloor,K-1\right\}
\]
is measurable and satisfies
\[
\Delta_K(H)\leq\frac{\ell}{2\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)K},
\qquad
D_H(g)\leq\frac{\ell}{2\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)K}.
\]

7656b93ab981f6f99e3f38f3a37a7ba3262d685a.title: Sharp fixed released law bounds
7656b93ab981f6f99e3f38f3a37a7ba3262d685a.body:
Let \(H\) be a measure on the score interval \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), let \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_J\) be a release rule, and let \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}\) be a measure on the released label, treatment arm, and outcome. Suppose:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The score support satisfies \cref{obj:ass:overlap}.
\item \textbf{(Release.)} The rule \(g\) is measurable.
\item \textbf{(Compatibility.)} \(\mathfrak M(H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\ne\varnothing\).
\end{itemize}

For each arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and label \(r\), let \(C_r=\{e:g(e)=r\}\), let \(p_a(e)\) be the probability of arm \(a\) at score \(e\), and set \(q_{ar}=\int_{C_r}p_a(e)\,H(de)\). In each cell with \(q_{ar}>0\), let \(F_{ar}\) be the outcome law conditional on arm \(a\) and label \(r\) under \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}\), let \(E_{ar}\) have law \(q_{ar}^{-1}\mathbf 1_{C_r}(e)p_a(e)\,H(de)\), and let \(W_{ar}=1/p_a(E_{ar})\). Writing \(Q\) for a generalized quantile, define
\[
\underline\mu_a
=\sum_{r:q_{ar}>0}q_{ar}\int_0^1 Q_{F_{ar}}(u)Q_{W_{ar}}(1-u)\,du,
\qquad
\overline\mu_a
=\sum_{r:q_{ar}>0}q_{ar}\int_0^1 Q_{F_{ar}}(u)Q_{W_{ar}}(u)\,du.
\]
Then, for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\left\{\mathbb E_P[Y_a]:P\in\mathfrak M(H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\right\}
=[\underline\mu_a,\overline\mu_a].
\]
The attainable average treatment effects form the interval defined in \cref{obj:def:sharp-ate-set}:
\[
\left\{\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0]:P\in\mathfrak M(H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\right\}
=I(P_{\mathrm{rel}};H,g)
=[\underline\mu_1-\overline\mu_0,\,
  \overline\mu_1-\underline\mu_0].
\]
Moreover, there exist \(P^-,P^+\in\mathfrak M(H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\) such that
\[
\mathbb E_{P^-}[Y_1-Y_0]=\underline\mu_1-\overline\mu_0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_{P^+}[Y_1-Y_0]=\overline\mu_1-\underline\mu_0.
\]

ed550b2fd142c716aca873299c525ce24eafd0ae.title: Exact all-label ambiguity width
ed550b2fd142c716aca873299c525ce24eafd0ae.body:
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap condition in \cref{obj:ass:overlap} holds.
\item \textbf{(Score law.)} \(H\) is a probability law on \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
\item \textbf{(Release.)} \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_J\) is measurable.
\end{itemize}
Write \(C_r=\{e:g(e)=r\}\), \(p_1(e)=e\), \(p_0(e)=1-e\), and \(q_{ar}=\int_{C_r}p_a(e)\,H(de)\). Let \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}\) be the released law
\[
P_{\mathrm{rel}}
=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_J}\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}
\frac{q_{ar}}{2}\bigl(\delta_{(r,a,0)}+\delta_{(r,a,1)}\bigr).
\]
Thus its observed outcome law \(F_{ar}\) is Bernoulli\((1/2)\) in every positive-mass arm-label cell.

The worst-case ambiguity \(D_H(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:worst-case-ambiguity} satisfies
\[
D_H(g)=
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_J}
\left[
\inf_{c\in[1/(1-\varepsilon),\,1/\varepsilon]}
\int_{C_r}|1-ce|\,H(de)
+
\inf_{c\in[1/(1-\varepsilon),\,1/\varepsilon]}
\int_{C_r}|1-c(1-e)|\,H(de)
\right].
\]

For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and each cell with \(q_{ar}>0\), let \(E_{ar}\) have law \(p_a(e)\mathbf 1_{C_r}(e)H(de)/q_{ar}\), and let \(W_{ar}=1/p_a(E_{ar})\). Define
\[
\underline\mu_a
=\sum_{r:q_{ar}>0}q_{ar}\int_0^1
Q_{F_{ar}}(u)Q_{W_{ar}}(1-u)\,du,
\qquad
\overline\mu_a
=\sum_{r:q_{ar}>0}q_{ar}\int_0^1
Q_{F_{ar}}(u)Q_{W_{ar}}(u)\,du.
\]
The sharp ATE interval for \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}\) has length \(D_H(g)\). Moreover, there are two probability laws \(P_-,P_+\in\mathfrak M(H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\), as defined in \cref{obj:def:compatible-law-class}, such that
\[
\mathbb E_{P_-}[Y_1-Y_0]=\underline\mu_1-\overline\mu_0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_{P_+}[Y_1-Y_0]=\overline\mu_1-\underline\mu_0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_{P_+}[Y_1-Y_0]-\mathbb E_{P_-}[Y_1-Y_0]=D_H(g).
\]

a1fa8ff45c3a9d1c74a97454b80264bbb5124540.title: Minimax honest interval length
a1fa8ff45c3a9d1c74a97454b80264bbb5124540.body:
Fix an overlap parameter \(\varepsilon\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:overlap}\) and a miscoverage level \(0<\alpha<1/2\). Let \(\mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\) and \(\mathcal J_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\) be as in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-honest-length,obj:def:honest-procedures}\). There are positive constants \(C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\) and \(c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\) such that, for every score probability law \(H\) on \(\mathcal E\) and every \(n,K\geq1\),
\[
c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}n^{-1/2}
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H).
\]

For every \(m_f>0\), there is a positive constant \(c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}\) such that, for every \(H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:score-lower-density-class}\) and every \(n,K\geq1\),
\[
c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr)
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

The upper bound has the following construction. For the equal-width release \(g_K\), the label assigned to a score \(e\in\mathcal E\) is
\[
g_K(e)=\min\left\{\left\lfloor
\frac{K(e-\varepsilon)}{1-2\varepsilon}
\right\rfloor,K-1\right\},
\qquad
z_r=\varepsilon+\frac{(r+1/2)(1-2\varepsilon)}{K},
\quad r=0,\ldots,K-1.
\]
For released trial rows \((R_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\), define
\[
\widehat T_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left\{\frac{A_iY_i}{z_{R_i}}
-\frac{(1-A_i)Y_i}{1-z_{R_i}}\right\},
\qquad
R_{n,K}=\frac4\varepsilon
\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{n}}
+\frac{1-2\varepsilon}{2K\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)},
\qquad
\operatorname{clampATE}(t)=\max\{-1,\min\{1,t\}\}.
\]
Then the interval
\[
C_n=
\bigl[\operatorname{clampATE}(\widehat T_n-R_{n,K}),
      \operatorname{clampATE}(\widehat T_n+R_{n,K})\bigr]
\]
satisfies \((g_K,C_n)\in\mathcal J_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\). For every causal law \(P\in\mathfrak P(H,g_K)\), with \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}\) its released-row law,
\[
\int |C_n(x)|\,dP_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\otimes n}(x)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

b37bed63cad0091ef11d0b982bb8d4095f003be3.title: Paired high-resolution quantization
b37bed63cad0091ef11d0b982bb8d4095f003be3.body:
Let \(\mathcal I=[a,b]\), let \(S\) be a positive integer, and let \(\beta_s:\mathcal I\times\mathcal I\to\mathbb R\), \(s=1,\ldots,S\), satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nondegenerate interval.)} \(a<b\).
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} Each \(\beta_s\) is continuous on \(\mathcal I\times\mathcal I\).
\item \textbf{(Positivity.)} \(\beta_s(x,z)>0\) for every \(s\) and every \(x,z\in\mathcal I\).
\end{itemize}
For each positive integer \(k\), define the minimum achievable cost over ordered interval partitions of \(\mathcal I\) and reproduction points in \(\mathcal I\) by
\[
V_k=\inf_{\substack{(B_1,\ldots,B_k)\ \mathrm{ordered\ interval\ partition\ of}\ \mathcal I\\ z_{js}\in\mathcal I}}
\sum_{j=1}^{k}\sum_{s=1}^{S}
\int_{B_j}\beta_s(x,z_{js})|x-z_{js}|\,dx,
\qquad
w(x)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\beta_s(x,x).
\]
Then
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty} kV_k
=\frac14\left(\int_a^b\sqrt{w(x)}\,dx\right)^2.
\]
For each positive integer \(k\), choose boundaries \(a=t_0<\cdots<t_k=b\) satisfying
\[
\int_a^{t_j}\sqrt{w(x)}\,dx
=\frac{j}{k}\int_a^b\sqrt{w(x)}\,dx
\qquad (j=0,\ldots,k),
\]
and set \(B_j=[t_{j-1},t_j)\) for \(j<k\), \(B_k=[t_{k-1},t_k]\), and \(z_{js}=(t_{j-1}+t_j)/2\) for every \(s\). These cells form an ordered interval partition of \(\mathcal I\), every \(z_{js}\) belongs to \(\mathcal I\), and their cost satisfies
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}
k\sum_{j=1}^{k}\sum_{s=1}^{S}
\int_{B_j}\beta_s(x,z_{js})|x-z_{js}|\,dx
=\frac14\left(\int_a^b\sqrt{w(x)}\,dx\right)^2.
\]

c798b9d0e01d9613d5d2ba514f6d46894cf29bc9.title: Sharp high resolution constant
c798b9d0e01d9613d5d2ba514f6d46894cf29bc9.body:
Let \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) be the score interval, and let \(H\) be a probability law on \(\mathcal E\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap condition in \cref{obj:ass:overlap} holds.
\item \textbf{(Density.)} \(H(de)=f(e)\,de\) on \(\mathcal E\).
\item \textbf{(Regularity.)} The density \(f\) is continuous and strictly positive on \(\mathcal E\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\Delta_K(H)\) and \(D_H(g)\) be the optimal \(K\)-label ambiguity and the worst-case ambiguity defined in \cref{obj:def:optimal-k-ambiguity,obj:def:worst-case-ambiguity}. For every positive integer \(K\), there is a measurable release \(g_K:\mathcal E\to\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\) whose label cells are intervals, such that
\[
\lim_{K\to\infty}K\Delta_K(H)
=
\lim_{K\to\infty}K D_H(g_K)
=
\frac14\left(
\int_{\varepsilon}^{1-\varepsilon}
\sqrt{\frac{f(e)}{e(1-e)}}\,de
\right)^2.
\]

e8ceac19efb9cb269312c501d42effed689aaa4b.title: External-score root order
e8ceac19efb9cb269312c501d42effed689aaa4b.body:
Let \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), and let \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_J\) be a measurable finite-label release. Suppose:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap condition in \cref{obj:ass:overlap} holds.
\item \textbf{(Miscoverage.)} \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Joint sampling.)} For every \(n,m\), a joint sampling law \(\mathbb Q_{P,H}^{n,m}\) is specified for each admissible causal law \(P\) and score law \(H\). Its trial marginal consists of \(n\) independent draws from the released law. Its score-log marginal and independence from the trial sample satisfy \cref{obj:ass:external-log-iid,obj:ass:external-log-independent}.
\end{itemize}

Set
\[
L_\alpha=1+(1-2\alpha)^2,\qquad
S_g=
\sup_{\substack{r\in\mathcal R_J,\ e_1<e_2<e_3\\
e_1,e_2,e_3\in C_r}}
\frac{(e_3-e_2)(1-e_1/e_2)}
{\sqrt{(e_3-e_2)^2+(e_3-e_1)^2+(e_2-e_1)^2}},
\]
and
\[
c_{\mathrm{tr}}(\alpha)
=\frac{(1-2\alpha)\sqrt{\log L_\alpha}}{4},
\qquad
c_{\mathrm{log}}(g,\alpha)
=\frac{(1-2\alpha)\sqrt{\log L_\alpha}}{2\sqrt3}\,S_g.
\]
Then \(0<S_g\le 1\). There is a constant \(C_{\varepsilon,J,\alpha,g}>0\) such that, for every positive \(n,m\), the minimax excess risk of \cref{obj:def:external-excess-risk} satisfies
\[
c_{\mathrm{tr}}(\alpha)n^{-1/2}
\le \mathcal R^\star_{n,m,\alpha}(g)
\le C_{\varepsilon,J,\alpha,g}
\bigl(n^{-1/2}+m^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]
For each such \(n,m\), an interval procedure \(C_{n,m}\) belongs to the honest class of \cref{obj:def:external-honest-procedures}, agrees pointwise as a closed interval with the projection interval of \cref{obj:def:external-projection-handle}, and, for every admissible pair \((P,H)\), satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{P,H}^{n,m}}
\!\left[
\max\!\left\{0,\,
\operatorname{length}(C_{n,m})
-\operatorname{length}\bigl(I(P_{\mathrm{rel}};H,g)\bigr)
\right\}
\right]
\le C_{\varepsilon,J,\alpha,g}
\bigl(n^{-1/2}+m^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

In the external-score direction,
\[
\liminf_{m\to\infty}\inf_{n\ge1}
\sqrt m\,\mathcal R^\star_{n,m,\alpha}(g)
\ge c_{\mathrm{log}}(g,\alpha)>0.
\]
For every \(\rho>0\), the normalized risk \(T_{n,m,\alpha}(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:external-normalized-risk} obeys
\[
0<
\max\left\{
\frac{c_{\mathrm{tr}}(\alpha)}{1+\sqrt\rho},
\frac{c_{\mathrm{log}}(g,\alpha)\sqrt\rho}{1+\sqrt\rho}
\right\}
\le
\liminf_{\substack{n,m\to\infty\\ n/m\to\rho}}
T_{n,m,\alpha}(g)
\le
\limsup_{\substack{n,m\to\infty\\ n/m\to\rho}}
T_{n,m,\alpha}(g)
\le C_{\varepsilon,J,\alpha,g}.
\]

3be3a230666f0d653f5bc3aa52f6d7c865b16577.title: Two-source excess-risk lower bounds
3be3a230666f0d653f5bc3aa52f6d7c865b16577.body:
Let \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) be the score interval, let \(\mathcal R_J\) be the finite label set, and fix a measurable release \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_J\). Let \(\mathbb Q_{P,H}^{n,m}\) be a family of joint sampling laws on \(n\) released trial rows and \(m\) score-log draws. Suppose:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap and level.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:overlap}\) holds and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Trial sampling.)} For every \(n,m\) and every admissible causal-law and score-law pair \((P,H)\) under \(g\), the trial marginal of \(\mathbb Q_{P,H}^{n,m}\) is the \(n\)-fold product of the released-row law under \(P\).
\item \textbf{(Score-log sampling.)} The joint sampling laws satisfy \(\cref{obj:ass:external-log-iid,obj:ass:external-log-independent}\) for every \(n,m\).
\end{itemize}

Set
\[
L_\alpha=1+(1-2\alpha)^2,\qquad
S_g=\sup_{\substack{r\in\mathcal R_J,\ e_1,e_2,e_3\in\mathcal E\\
e_1<e_2<e_3,\ g(e_1)=g(e_2)=g(e_3)=r}}
\frac{(e_3-e_2)(1-e_1/e_2)}
{\sqrt{(e_3-e_2)^2+(e_3-e_1)^2+(e_2-e_1)^2}},
\]
and
\[
c_{\mathrm{tr}}(\alpha)
=\frac{(1-2\alpha)\sqrt{\log L_\alpha}}{4},
\qquad
c_{\mathrm{log}}(g,\alpha)
=\frac{(1-2\alpha)\sqrt{\log L_\alpha}}{2\sqrt{3}}S_g.
\]
Then \(0<S_g\leq 1\). The external-score minimax excess risk of \(\cref{obj:def:external-excess-risk}\) satisfies, for every \(n,m\geq 1\),
\[
\mathcal R^\star_{n,m,\alpha}(g)
\geq \frac{c_{\mathrm{tr}}(\alpha)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
It also satisfies
\[
\liminf_{m\to\infty}\inf_{n\geq 1}
\left\{\sqrt m\,\mathcal R^\star_{n,m,\alpha}(g)\right\}
\geq c_{\mathrm{log}}(g,\alpha)>0.
\]
For every \(\rho>0\), the normalized risk of \(\cref{obj:def:external-normalized-risk}\) satisfies
\[
\liminf_{\substack{n,m\to\infty\\ n/m\to\rho}}
T_{n,m,\alpha}(g)
\geq
\max\left\{
\frac{c_{\mathrm{tr}}(\alpha)}{1+\sqrt\rho},
\frac{c_{\mathrm{log}}(g,\alpha)\sqrt\rho}{1+\sqrt\rho}
\right\}>0.
\]

2bf59c463da03dded8ce74896288d778c49f5ca6.title: Score marginal law
2bf59c463da03dded8ce74896288d778c49f5ca6.body:
The score \(E\) has law \(H\) under \(P\):
\[
\mathcal L_P(E)=H.
\]

cb42713751565bfa79f15327afb1ec9ae10e60b4.title: Arm-cell quantities $p_a,C_r,q_{ar},F_{ar},G_{ar},E_{ar},W_{ar}$
cb42713751565bfa79f15327afb1ec9ae10e60b4.body:
For each arm \(a\in\mathcal A\) and label \(r\in\mathcal R_J\), define
\[
p_1(e)=e,\qquad p_0(e)=1-e,\qquad
C_r=\{e:g(e)=r\},\qquad
q_{ar}=\int_{C_r}p_a(e)\,H(de).
\]
When \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}(A=a,R=r)>0\), define the observed outcome law
\[
F_{ar}=\mathcal L_{P_{\mathrm{rel}}}(Y\mid A=a,R=r).
\]
For \(q_{ar}>0\), define
\[
G_{ar}(de)=\frac{\mathbf 1\{e\in C_r\}p_a(e)\,H(de)}{q_{ar}},
\qquad E_{ar}\sim G_{ar},
\qquad W_{ar}=\frac{1}{p_a(E_{ar})}.
\]
The endpoint formulas apply to triples \((H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\) satisfying \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}(A=a,R=r)=q_{ar}\) for every arm and label. Their sums include cells with \(q_{ar}>0\), for which \(F_{ar}\) is defined.

36c7a04266914489d68b89fc13657dc320666275.title: Mean endpoints $\underline\mu_a,\overline\mu_a$
36c7a04266914489d68b89fc13657dc320666275.body:
For a triple \((H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\) satisfying \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}(A=a,R=r)=q_{ar}\) for every arm and label, define
\[
\underline\mu_a
=\sum_{r:q_{ar}>0}q_{ar}\int_0^1
Q_{F_{ar}}(u)Q_{W_{ar}}(1-u)\,du,
\qquad
\overline\mu_a
=\sum_{r:q_{ar}>0}q_{ar}\int_0^1
Q_{F_{ar}}(u)Q_{W_{ar}}(u)\,du.
\]

1f5d017deada5553d9291a292f0717608901c10a.title: Uniformly honest procedures $\mathcal J_{n,K,\alpha}(H)$
1f5d017deada5553d9291a292f0717608901c10a.body:
\[
\mathcal J_{n,K,\alpha}(H)
=
\left\{
(g,C_n):
g\in\mathcal G_K,\quad
\inf_{P\in\mathfrak P(H,g)}
P^{\otimes n}\!\left[
\theta(P)\in C_n\bigl((R_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\bigr)
\right]
\ge 1-\alpha
\right\}.
\]

6e7177cedfb2bb8924d494a3e0a6d1ba2c56880f.title: High-resolution handle $\mathsf H_{\mathrm{opt}}$
6e7177cedfb2bb8924d494a3e0a6d1ba2c56880f.body: The high-resolution handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{opt}}\) consists of an uncrossing or intervalization result for the paired reciprocal-score absolute-deviation loss in \(D_H(g)\), followed by local one-dimensional quantization arguments for the resulting ordered cells.

cc46e884461f86c1e0b053ca6b647600cf799672.title: External law class $\mathfrak X(g)$
cc46e884461f86c1e0b053ca6b647600cf799672.body:
\[
\mathfrak X(g)
=
\left\{
(P,H):
H\in\mathcal P(\mathcal E),\quad
P\in\mathfrak P(H,g)
\right\}.
\]
The class uses the conditions in \cref{obj:ass:overlap,obj:ass:score-marginal,obj:ass:randomized-assignment,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:deterministic-release}.

814ca317a643b538f1349b3d12092f4e5b062b2e.title: External experiment $\mathbb Q_{P,H}^{n,m}$
814ca317a643b538f1349b3d12092f4e5b062b2e.body:
For \((P,H)\in\mathfrak X(g)\), the joint law of \(n\) released trial observations \((R_i,A_i,Y_i)\) and \(m\) independent score-log observations \(E_j^{\mathrm{log}}\) is
\[
\mathbb Q_{P,H}^{n,m}
=
\mathcal L_P(R,A,Y)^{\otimes n}\otimes H^{\otimes m}.
\]

9f0fc362045f052163ff49c627b608d7dde1384c.title: Lower bound on score density
9f0fc362045f052163ff49c627b608d7dde1384c.body:
The score law \(H\) has density \(f\) on the score interval \(\mathcal E\), with
\[
H(de)=f(e)\,de,\qquad f(e)\ge m_f
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(e\in\mathcal E\).

f0320b8957ff5c56a6eae87ae55e5fbcfaff6c39.title: Independent trial sampling
f0320b8957ff5c56a6eae87ae55e5fbcfaff6c39.body:
The trial observations are independent and identically distributed under \(P\):
\[
(R_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal L_P(R,A,Y).
\]

f0af5351d7da42b71173c1ea77063d01e7ba9b19.title: Independent score-log sampling
f0af5351d7da42b71173c1ea77063d01e7ba9b19.body:
The external score-log observations are independent and identically distributed with law \(H\):
\[
(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})_{j=1}^m\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}H.
\]

5bfc85c20efa8bad6d256df0e491f272fd726e6c.title: Independent trial and score log
5bfc85c20efa8bad6d256df0e491f272fd726e6c.body:
The external score log is independent of the trial observations:
\[
(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})_{j=1}^m
\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}
(R_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n.
\]

c50c5d4bb6d611ef7cba16c894762a43e3a60802.title: Causal-law class \(\mathfrak P(H,g)\)
c50c5d4bb6d611ef7cba16c894762a43e3a60802.body: The causal-law class \(\mathfrak P(H,g)\) consists of all laws \(P\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:score-marginal,obj:ass:randomized-assignment,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:deterministic-release}.

9ed59a77f28d3d5c1614a5fc82e845599873ef12.title: Compatible-law class \(\mathfrak M(H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})\)
9ed59a77f28d3d5c1614a5fc82e845599873ef12.body:
The compatible-law class is
\[
\mathfrak M(H,g,P_{\mathrm{rel}})
=
\bigl\{P\in\mathfrak P(H,g):\mathcal L_P(R,A,Y)=P_{\mathrm{rel}}\bigr\}.
\]
Here \(\mathfrak P(H,g)\) imposes \cref{obj:ass:score-marginal,obj:ass:randomized-assignment,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:deterministic-release}, and the released-law condition is \cref{obj:ass:released-law}.

f00cd76415c08ee56e1e9da6c0570a27c8ef4ef6.title: Minimax external excess risk $\mathcal R^{\star}_{n,m,\alpha}(g)$
f00cd76415c08ee56e1e9da6c0570a27c8ef4ef6.body:
\[
\mathcal R^{\star}_{n,m,\alpha}(g)
=
\inf_{C_{n,m}\in\mathcal J^{\mathrm{ext}}_{n,m,\alpha}(g)}
\sup_{(P,H)\in\mathfrak X(g)}
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{P,H}^{n,m}}
\!\left[
\left(
\operatorname{len}(C_{n,m})
-
\operatorname{len}I(\mathcal L_P(R,A,Y);H,g)
\right)_+
\right].
\]

c77acdfc55d1eebf1923c57226fbb8805d5b57c6.title: External projection interval $C_{n,m}$
c77acdfc55d1eebf1923c57226fbb8805d5b57c6.body:
Given \(n\) trial rows, \(m\) independent score-log draws, a measurable release \(g\) with \(J\) labels, an overlap parameter \(\varepsilon\), and a confidence level \(1-\alpha\), construct \(C_{n,m}\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Form the empirical finite measures, for each arm \(a\) and label \(r\):
\[
\widehat\lambda_{ar}(B)
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{R_i=r,A_i=a,Y_i\in B\},
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_{ar}(B)
=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^{m}p_a(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})
\mathbf 1\{g(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})=r,E_j^{\mathrm{log}}\in B\}.
\]
Equip finite measures on each compact support with total-mass plus integrated-CDF distance, and set
\[
r_n=\frac{4J}{\alpha\sqrt n},
\qquad
r_m=\frac{2J(2-2\varepsilon)}{\alpha\sqrt m}.
\]

\item Under the standing overlap condition, form the rational sieve \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}\). For \(q,w\in\mathbb Q\), define
\[
x(q)=\max\{0,\min\{1,q\}\},
\qquad
e_\varepsilon(q)=\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)x(q),
\qquad
\operatorname{ofReal}(w)=\max\{w,0\}.
\]
For each finite list \(L=((q_s,w_s))_{s=1}^{N}\), let
\[
\nu_Y(L)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\operatorname{ofReal}(w_s)\delta_{x(q_s)},
\qquad
\nu_E(L)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\operatorname{ofReal}(w_s)\delta_{e_\varepsilon(q_s)}.
\]
The weights are viewed as nonnegative extended-real weights. With separate, arbitrary outcome and score lists \(L^Y,L^E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal R_J\to\operatorname{List}(\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q)\), set
\[
\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}
=
\left\{
\left(
(\nu_Y(L^Y_{ar}))_{a,r},
(\nu_E(L^E_{ar}))_{a,r}
\right):
\operatorname{ProjectionCompatible}
\left(
(\nu_Y(L^Y_{ar}))_{a,r},
(\nu_E(L^E_{ar}))_{a,r}
\right)
\right\}.
\]
Compatibility imposes exact equality of the outcome and score measures’ total masses in every arm-label cell. Duplicate support codes, codes clamped from outside \([0,1]\), and nonpositive weights leave the represented nonnegative measures unchanged. If overlap fails, set \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}=\varnothing\).

\item Retain the compatible sieve arrays in both closed empirical balls:
\[
\mathcal B_{n,m}
=
\left\{
(\lambda',\sigma')\in\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}:
\sum_{a,r}d_{[0,1]}(\lambda'_{ar},\widehat\lambda_{ar})\le r_n,\quad
\sum_{a,r}d_{\mathcal E}(\sigma'_{ar},\widehat\sigma_{ar})\le r_m
\right\}.
\]

\item For each \(b\in\mathcal B_{n,m}\), compute its two quantile-transport average treatment effect endpoints and the resulting interval \(I(b)\). When \(\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\), form
\[
J_{n,m}
=
[-1,1]\cap
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}
\left(\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal B_{n,m}}I(b)\right).
\]

\item Return
\[
C_{n,m}
=
\begin{cases}
J_{n,m},&
\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\ \text{and}\ J_{n,m}\ne\varnothing,\\
\{0\},&
\mathcal B_{n,m}=\varnothing\ \text{or}\
\bigl(\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\ \text{and}\ J_{n,m}=\varnothing\bigr).
\end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}
This totalized rational-sieve rule is measurable and attains the external-score root order, including for laws with atoms.

7e60338ccd6c2f08bb6ae30cd6a27caba3d6c087.title: Lower-density score class $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}$
7e60338ccd6c2f08bb6ae30cd6a27caba3d6c087.body:
Under \cref{obj:ass:density-lower}, the class of score laws is
\[
\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}
=
\left\{
H\in\mathcal P(\mathcal E):
H(de)=f(e)\,de,\quad
f(e)\ge m_f\ \text{for Lebesgue-almost every }e\in\mathcal E
\right\}.
\]

b41c4a93e316cfc39f01d1ac9f2c0b4901f881af.title: External-score sharp limits
b41c4a93e316cfc39f01d1ac9f2c0b4901f881af.body:
Fix a measurable release \(g\), \(0<\alpha<1/2\), and \(\rho\in(0,\infty)\). The sharp asymptotic analysis over \(\mathfrak X(g)\), with confidence procedures in \(\mathcal J^{\mathrm{ext}}_{n,m,\alpha}(g)\), concerns
\[
\liminf_{\substack{n,m\to\infty\\ n/m\to\rho}}T_{n,m,\alpha}(g)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\limsup_{\substack{n,m\to\infty\\ n/m\to\rho}}T_{n,m,\alpha}(g).
\]
It asks whether these limits coincide and, if so, for their common sharp constant. If a common sharp limit fails over the full class, the corresponding question concerns an explicitly defined regular subclass of \(\mathfrak X(g)\), with both uniform honesty and the supremum in expected excess length restricted to that subclass. The subclass analysis specifies its regularity conditions and sharp limit for each \(\rho\in(0,\infty)\), using the external projection construction to obtain an attaining procedure or a counterexample.

c087391df637221f0d3943bae16b49846d85abc4.title: Average treatment effect functional
c087391df637221f0d3943bae16b49846d85abc4.body:
For any measure \(P\) on full rows \((E,Y_0,Y_1,A,Y,R)\) with score parameter \(\varepsilon\) and \(J\) labels, define the average treatment effect functional \(\theta(P)\) by
\[
\theta(P)=\int (Y_1-Y_0)\,dP.
\]

0684cfa05ebf67daf16226de795d6069810e03be.title: Paired high-resolution quantization
0684cfa05ebf67daf16226de795d6069810e03be.body:
Let \(\mathcal I=[a,b]\), let \(S\) be an integer, and let \(\beta_s:\mathcal I\times\mathcal I\to\mathbb R\), \(s=1,\ldots,S\), satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Interval.)} \(a<b\).
\item \textbf{(Number of components.)} \(S\geq1\).
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} Each \(\beta_s\) is continuous on \(\mathcal I\times\mathcal I\).
\item \textbf{(Positivity.)} \(\beta_s(x,z)>0\) for every \(s\) and every \(x,z\in\mathcal I\).
\end{itemize}
For each positive integer \(k\), define
\[
V_k=
\inf_{\substack{(B_1,\ldots,B_k)\ \mathrm{measurable,\ pairwise\ disjoint}\\
\bigcup_{j=1}^{k}B_j=\mathcal I,\quad z_{js}\in\mathcal I}}
\sum_{j=1}^{k}\sum_{s=1}^{S}
\int_{B_j}\beta_s(x,z_{js})|x-z_{js}|\,dx,
\qquad
w(x)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\beta_s(x,x).
\]
Then
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}kV_k
=\frac14\left(\int_a^b\sqrt{w(x)}\,dx\right)^2.
\]
For each positive integer \(k\), let \(a=t_0<\cdots<t_k=b\) be boundaries satisfying
\[
\int_a^{t_j}\sqrt{w(x)}\,dx
=\frac{j}{k}\int_a^b\sqrt{w(x)}\,dx
\qquad (j=0,\ldots,k).
\]
Set \(B_j=[t_{j-1},t_j)\) for \(j<k\), \(B_k=[t_{k-1},t_k]\), and \(z_{js}=(t_{j-1}+t_j)/2\) for every \(s\). These cells form a measurable, pairwise-disjoint partition of \(\mathcal I\), every \(z_{js}\) belongs to \(\mathcal I\), and
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}
k\sum_{j=1}^{k}\sum_{s=1}^{S}
\int_{B_j}\beta_s(x,z_{js})|x-z_{js}|\,dx
=\frac14\left(\int_a^b\sqrt{w(x)}\,dx\right)^2.
\]

38bc323e3dfb5bfb49336098dce53b7f69b767d9.title: Minimax honest interval length
38bc323e3dfb5bfb49336098dce53b7f69b767d9.body:
Consider the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap parameter \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:overlap}.
\item \textbf{(Miscoverage.)} \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Score law.)} \(H\) is a probability law on the score interval \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
\item \textbf{(Trial size.)} \(n\geq1\).
\item \textbf{(Label budget.)} \(K\geq1\).
\end{itemize}
There are constants \(C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}>0\) and \(c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}>0\), independent of \(H,n,K\), such that every \(H,n,K\) satisfying these conditions obeys
\[
c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}n^{-1/2}
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H),
\]
where \(\mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\) is defined in \cref{obj:def:minimax-honest-length}.

For every \(m_f>0\), there is a constant \(c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}>0\) such that, for every \(H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:score-lower-density-class} and every \(n,K\geq1\),
\[
c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr)
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

The upper bound is attained by an honest interval paired with the equal-width release
\[
g_K(e)=\min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac{K(e-\varepsilon)}{1-2\varepsilon}\right\rfloor,K-1\right\},
\qquad
z_r=\varepsilon+\frac{(r+1/2)(1-2\varepsilon)}{K},
\quad r=0,\ldots,K-1.
\]
For released trial rows \((R_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\), set
\[
\widehat T_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left\{\frac{A_iY_i}{z_{R_i}}-\frac{(1-A_i)Y_i}{1-z_{R_i}}\right\},
\qquad
R_{n,K}=\frac4\varepsilon\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{n}}
+\frac{1-2\varepsilon}{2K\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)},
\qquad
\operatorname{clampATE}(t)=\max\{-1,\min\{1,t\}\}.
\]
The interval
\[
C_n=
\bigl[\operatorname{clampATE}(\widehat T_n-R_{n,K}),
      \operatorname{clampATE}(\widehat T_n+R_{n,K})\bigr]
\]
satisfies \((g_K,C_n)\in\mathcal J_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\), with honesty as defined in \cref{obj:def:honest-procedures}. For every \(P\in\mathfrak P(H,g_K)\), as defined in \cref{obj:def:causal-law-class}, its expected length under the \(n\)-fold released-row law satisfies
\[
\int |C_n(x)|\,dP_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\otimes n}(x)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

995a72a2ace83dbc98a06bd8eaf5515b3cb197de.title: Totalized external projection interval
995a72a2ace83dbc98a06bd8eaf5515b3cb197de.body:
For a score interval \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), a release \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_J\), sample sizes \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), a real number \(\alpha\), and a sample consisting of \(n\) trial rows and \(m\) score-log values, define \(C_{n,m}\) as follows.

For each arm \(a\) and label \(r\), form the empirical finite measures
\[
\widehat\lambda_{ar}(B)
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{R_i=r,A_i=a,Y_i\in B\},
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_{ar}(B)
=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^{m}p_a(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})
\mathbf 1\{g(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})=r,E_j^{\mathrm{log}}\in B\}.
\]
Use total-mass plus integrated-CDF distance \(d_{[0,1]}\) for outcome measures and \(d_{\mathcal E}\) for score measures, with radii
\[
r_n=\frac{4J}{\alpha\sqrt n},
\qquad
r_m=\frac{2J(2-2\varepsilon)}{\alpha\sqrt m}.
\]

For \(q,w\in\mathbb Q\), set
\[
x(q)=\max\{0,\min\{1,q\}\},
\qquad
e_\varepsilon(q)=\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)x(q),
\qquad
w_+=\max\{w,0\}.
\]
Each finite list \(L=((q_s,w_s))_{s=1}^{N}\) of rational support-weight pairs represents the finite measures
\[
\nu_Y(L)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}(w_s)_+\delta_{x(q_s)},
\qquad
\nu_E(L)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}(w_s)_+\delta_{e_\varepsilon(q_s)},
\]
where the weights are interpreted as nonnegative extended-real weights. When \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), let \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}\) contain every pair of arm-label arrays
\[
\left((\nu_Y(L^Y_{ar}))_{a,r},(\nu_E(L^E_{ar}))_{a,r}\right)
\]
formed from separate, arbitrary finite rational support-weight lists \(L^Y_{ar}\) and \(L^E_{ar}\) whose outcome and score measures have equal total mass in every arm-label cell. When \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) fails, set \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}=\varnothing\).

Retain the sieve arrays satisfying both closed empirical-ball inequalities:
\[
\mathcal B_{n,m}
=
\left\{
(\lambda',\sigma')\in\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}:
\sum_{a,r}d_{[0,1]}(\lambda'_{ar},\widehat\lambda_{ar})\le r_n,\quad
\sum_{a,r}d_{\mathcal E}(\sigma'_{ar},\widehat\sigma_{ar})\le r_m
\right\}.
\]
For each \(b\in\mathcal B_{n,m}\), let \(I(b)\) be the interval between its two quantile-transport average treatment effect endpoints. When \(\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\), set
\[
J_{n,m}
=
[-1,1]\cap
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}
\left(\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal B_{n,m}}I(b)\right).
\]
The totalized external projection interval is
\[
C_{n,m}
=
\begin{cases}
J_{n,m},&
\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\ \text{and}\ J_{n,m}\ne\varnothing,\\
\{0\},&
\mathcal B_{n,m}=\varnothing\ \text{or}\
\bigl(\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\ \text{and}\ J_{n,m}=\varnothing\bigr).
\end{cases}
\]

8d14d3a957b593938b5db9fdb1d72b934b90740c.title: Released arm-cell masses
8d14d3a957b593938b5db9fdb1d72b934b90740c.body:
Let \(H\) be a measure on the score interval \(\mathcal E\), let \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_J\) be a release rule, and let \(P\in\mathfrak P(H,g)\) as in \cref{obj:def:causal-law-class}. Write \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}=\mathcal L_P(R,A,Y)\) for the released law. Then \(H\) and \(P_{\mathrm{rel}}\) are probability laws, and, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(r\in\mathcal R_J\),
\[
P_{\mathrm{rel}}(A=a,R=r)=q_{ar},
\]
where \(q_{ar}\) is the arm-cell mass defined in \cref{obj:def:arm-cell-primitives}.

f063900d1994d6c4481d78662c33791612aa3d2a.title: Minimax honest interval length
f063900d1994d6c4481d78662c33791612aa3d2a.body:
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap parameter \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:overlap}.
\item \textbf{(Miscoverage.)} \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Score law.)} \(H\) is a probability law on the score interval \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
\item \textbf{(Trial size.)} \(n\geq1\).
\item \textbf{(Label budget.)} \(K\geq1\).
\end{itemize}
There are constants \(C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}>0\) and \(c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}>0\), independent of \(H,n,K\), such that every \(H,n,K\) satisfying these conditions obeys
\[
c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}n^{-1/2}
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H),
\]
where \(\mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\) is defined in \cref{obj:def:minimax-honest-length}.

For every \(m_f>0\), there is a constant \(c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}>0\) such that, for every \(H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:score-lower-density-class} and every \(n,K\geq1\),
\[
c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr)
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

For the equal-width release, define
\[
g_K(e)=\min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac{K(e-\varepsilon)}{1-2\varepsilon}\right\rfloor,K-1\right\},
\qquad
z_r=\varepsilon+\frac{(r+1/2)(1-2\varepsilon)}{K},
\quad r=0,\ldots,K-1.
\]
For released trial rows \((R_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\), set

\[

\left[

\right]

\[
\int |C_n(x)|\,dP_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\otimes n}(x)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

\item \textbf{(Score law.)} \(H\) is a probability law on \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).

\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H),
\]
where \(\mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\) is defined in \cref{obj:def:minimax-honest-length}.

For every \(m_f>0\), there is a constant \(c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}>0\) such that, for every \(H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:score-lower-density-class} and every \(n,K\geq1\),
\[
c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr)
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

An honest interval satisfying the upper bound is paired with the equal-width release
\[
g_K(e)=\min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac{K(e-\varepsilon)}{1-2\varepsilon}\right\rfloor,K-1\right\},
\qquad
z_r=\varepsilon+\frac{(r+1/2)(1-2\varepsilon)}{K},
\quad r=0,\ldots,K-1.
\]
For released trial rows \((R_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\), set
\[
\widehat T_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left\{\frac{A_iY_i}{z_{R_i}}-\frac{(1-A_i)Y_i}{1-z_{R_i}}\right\},
\qquad
R_{n,K}=\frac4\varepsilon\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{n}}
+\frac{1-2\varepsilon}{2K\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)}.
\]
The interval
\[
C_n=
\left[
\max\{-1,\min\{1,\widehat T_n-R_{n,K}\}\},
\max\{-1,\min\{1,\widehat T_n+R_{n,K}\}\}
\right]
\]
satisfies \((g_K,C_n)\in\mathcal J_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\), with honesty as defined in \cref{obj:def:honest-procedures}. For every \(P\in\mathfrak P(H,g_K)\), as defined in \cref{obj:def:causal-law-class}, its expected length under the \(n\)-fold released-row law satisfies
\[
\int |C_n(x)|\,dP_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\otimes n}(x)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

0498eb3e6e03bc500fec49c0e9fec46bf32fc01a.title: External projection confidence interval
0498eb3e6e03bc500fec49c0e9fec46bf32fc01a.body:
The external projection interval \(C_{n,m}(g,\alpha;x)\) is defined for a release \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_J\), where \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) and \(\mathcal R_J\) is the set of \(J\) labels, a real number \(\alpha\), and data \(x\) comprising \(n\) trial rows and \(m\) score-log observations. Let \(\mathcal A\) be the set of treatment arms. For each \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(r\in\mathcal R_J\), form
\[
\widehat\lambda_{ar}(B)
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{R_i=r,A_i=a,Y_i\in B\},
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_{ar}(B)
=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^{m}p_a(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})
\mathbf 1\{g(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})=r,E_j^{\mathrm{log}}\in B\},
\]
with \(p_a\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:arm-cell-primitives}\). Equip finite measures on each compact support with total-mass plus integrated-CDF distance, denoted \(d_{[0,1]}\) and \(d_{\mathcal E}\), respectively, and set
\[
r_n=\frac{4J}{\alpha\sqrt n},
\qquad
r_m=\frac{2J(2-2\varepsilon)}{\alpha\sqrt m}.
\]

For rational \(q,w\), define
\[
x(q)=\max\{0,\min\{1,q\}\},
\qquad
e_\varepsilon(q)=\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)x(q).
\]
For a finite list \(L=((q_s,w_s))_{s=1}^{N}\) of rational pairs, define the finite measures
\[
\nu_Y(L)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\max\{w_s,0\}\,\delta_{x(q_s)},
\qquad
\nu_E(L)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\max\{w_s,0\}\,\delta_{e_\varepsilon(q_s)},
\]
where the weights are viewed as nonnegative extended-real numbers. When \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), let \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}\) consist of all arrays
\[
\left((\nu_Y(L^Y_{ar}))_{a,r},(\nu_E(L^E_{ar}))_{a,r}\right)
\]
formed from separate, arbitrary lists \(L^Y_{ar}\) and \(L^E_{ar}\), subject to equality of the outcome and score measures’ total masses in every arm-label cell. For other values of \(\varepsilon\), set \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}=\varnothing\).

Retain the arrays in both closed empirical balls:
\[
\mathcal B_{n,m}
=
\left\{
(\lambda',\sigma')\in\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}:
\sum_{a,r}d_{[0,1]}(\lambda'_{ar},\widehat\lambda_{ar})\le r_n,\quad
\sum_{a,r}d_{\mathcal E}(\sigma'_{ar},\widehat\sigma_{ar})\le r_m
\right\}.
\]
For each \(b\in\mathcal B_{n,m}\), let \(I(b)\) be the interval given by its two quantile-transport average treatment effect endpoints. When \(\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\), set
\[
J_{n,m}
=
[-1,1]\cap
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}
\left(\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal B_{n,m}}I(b)\right).
\]
The totalized interval is
\[
C_{n,m}(g,\alpha;x)
=
\begin{cases}
J_{n,m},&
\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\ \text{and}\ J_{n,m}\ne\varnothing,\\
\{0\},&
\mathcal B_{n,m}=\varnothing\ \text{or}\
\bigl(\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\ \text{and}\ J_{n,m}=\varnothing\bigr).
\end{cases}
\]

b1dd32e00226b302c15fbea4be5baa2fa7509fa6.title: Bounds for optimal label ambiguity
b1dd32e00226b302c15fbea4be5baa2fa7509fa6.body:
Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The condition in \cref{obj:ass:overlap} holds for \(\varepsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Density floor.)} \(m_f>0\).
\item \textbf{(Label budget.)} \(K\geq 1\) is an integer.
\end{itemize}
Let \(\ell=1-2\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). For every \(H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:score-lower-density-class},
\[
\frac{m_f\ell^2}{2(1-\varepsilon)K}\leq\Delta_K(H).
\]
For every probability law \(H\) on \(\mathcal E\), the equal-width release \(g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal R_K=\{1,\ldots,K\}\) defined by
\[
g(e)=1+\min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac{K(e-\varepsilon)}{\ell}\right\rfloor,K-1\right\}
\]
is measurable and satisfies
\[
\Delta_K(H)\leq\frac{\ell}{2\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)K},
\qquad
D_H(g)\leq\frac{\ell}{2\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)K}.
\]

00ff56026859adc65b062b3f8785b2d5249fe80f.title: Minimax honest interval length
00ff56026859adc65b062b3f8785b2d5249fe80f.body:
Consider the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap parameter \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:overlap}.
\item \textbf{(Miscoverage.)} \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Trial size.)} \(n\geq1\).
\item \textbf{(Label budget.)} \(K\geq1\).
\end{itemize}
There are constants \(C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}>0\) and \(c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}>0\), independent of \(H,n,K\), such that every score law \(H\) on \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) satisfies
\[
c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}n^{-1/2}
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H),
\]
where the minimax expected length is defined in \cref{obj:def:minimax-honest-length}.

For every \(m_f>0\), there is a constant \(c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}>0\) such that every \(H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\varepsilon,m_f}\), as defined in \cref{obj:def:score-lower-density-class}, satisfies
\[
c_{\varepsilon,m_f,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr)
\leq \mathcal L^\star_{n,K,\alpha}(H)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

An interval attaining the upper bound uses the equal-width release with labels \(r\in\mathcal R_K=\{1,\ldots,K\}\):
\[
g_K(e)=1+\min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac{K(e-\varepsilon)}{1-2\varepsilon}\right\rfloor,K-1\right\},
\qquad
z_r=\varepsilon+\frac{(r-\tfrac12)(1-2\varepsilon)}{K}.
\]
For released trial rows \((R_i,A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\), define
\[
\widehat T_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left\{\frac{A_iY_i}{z_{R_i}}-\frac{(1-A_i)Y_i}{1-z_{R_i}}\right\},
\qquad
R_{n,K}=\frac4\varepsilon\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{n}}
+\frac{1-2\varepsilon}{2K\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)}.
\]
With \(\operatorname{clampATE}(t)=\max\{-1,\min\{1,t\}\}\), the interval
\[
C_n(x)=
\left[
\operatorname{clampATE}\bigl(\widehat T_n(x)-R_{n,K}\bigr),
\operatorname{clampATE}\bigl(\widehat T_n(x)+R_{n,K}\bigr)
\right]
\]
satisfies \((g_K,C_n)\in\mathcal J_{n,K,\alpha}(H)\), with honesty defined in \cref{obj:def:honest-procedures}. For every \(P\in\mathfrak P(H,g_K)\), as defined in \cref{obj:def:causal-law-class}, its expected length under the \(n\)-fold released-row law satisfies
\[
\int |C_n(x)|\,dP_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\otimes n}(x)
\leq C_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\bigl(K^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\bigr).
\]

135aa2378e09a945d891c6f9587e0e90850ee422.title: External projection interval rule
135aa2378e09a945d891c6f9587e0e90850ee422.body:
For any \(\varepsilon,\alpha\in\mathbb R\), \(J,n,m\in\mathbb N\), release \(g:[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\to\mathcal R_J\), and sample consisting of \(n\) trial rows and \(m\) score-log entries, define the set \(C_{n,m}\) as follows. Here \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\) is the arm set and \(\mathcal R_J\) is the set of \(J\) labels. Reciprocals with zero denominator take the value zero.

For each arm \(a\) and label \(r\), form the empirical finite measures
\[
\widehat\lambda_{ar}(B)
=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{R_i=r,A_i=a,Y_i\in B\},
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_{ar}(B)
=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m}p_a(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})
\mathbf 1\{g(E_j^{\mathrm{log}})=r,E_j^{\mathrm{log}}\in B\},
\]
where \(p_a\) is the arm assignment probability from \(\cref{obj:def:arm-cell-primitives}\). Equip finite measures on the outcome interval \([0,1]\) and the score interval \(\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) with total-mass plus integrated-CDF distance, denoted respectively by \(d_{[0,1]}\) and \(d_{\mathcal E}\), and set
\[
r_n=\frac{4J}{\alpha\sqrt n},
\qquad
r_m=\frac{2J(2-2\varepsilon)}{\alpha\sqrt m}.
\]

For rational codes \(q,w\), define
\[
x(q)=\max\{0,\min\{1,q\}\},
\qquad
e_\varepsilon(q)=\varepsilon+(1-2\varepsilon)x(q),
\qquad
\operatorname{ofReal}(w)=\max\{w,0\}.
\]
The last expression is viewed as a nonnegative extended-real weight. For a finite list \(L=((q_s,w_s))_{s=1}^{N}\), let
\[
\nu_Y(L)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\operatorname{ofReal}(w_s)\delta_{x(q_s)},
\qquad
\nu_E(L)=\sum_{s=1}^{N}\operatorname{ofReal}(w_s)\delta_{e_\varepsilon(q_s)}.
\]
When \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), let \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}\) contain every pair of arrays
\[
\left((\nu_Y(L^Y_{ar}))_{a,r},(\nu_E(L^E_{ar}))_{a,r}\right)
\]
formed from arbitrary, separate lists \(L^Y,L^E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal R_J\to\operatorname{List}(\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q)\) for which the outcome and score measures have equal total mass in every arm-label cell. When \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) fails, set \(\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}=\varnothing\).

Retain the sieve arrays satisfying both closed empirical-ball inequalities:
\[
\mathcal B_{n,m}
=
\left\{
(\lambda',\sigma')\in\mathcal D_{\varepsilon,J}:
\sum_{a,r}d_{[0,1]}(\lambda'_{ar},\widehat\lambda_{ar})\le r_n,\quad
\sum_{a,r}d_{\mathcal E}(\sigma'_{ar},\widehat\sigma_{ar})\le r_m
\right\}.
\]
For each \(b\in\mathcal B_{n,m}\), let \(I(b)\) be the interval between its two quantile-transport average treatment effect endpoints. If \(\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\), put
\[
J_{n,m}
=
[-1,1]\cap
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}
\left(\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal B_{n,m}}I(b)\right).
\]
The external projection set is
\[
C_{n,m}
=
\begin{cases}
J_{n,m},&
\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\ \text{and}\ J_{n,m}\ne\varnothing,\\
\{0\},&
\mathcal B_{n,m}=\varnothing\ \text{or}\
\bigl(\mathcal B_{n,m}\ne\varnothing\ \text{and}\ J_{n,m}=\varnothing\bigr).
\end{cases}
\]

groups.title: Treatment-arm set
groups.body: The treatment-arm set is \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), where \(0\) denotes control and \(1\) denotes treatment.

groups.title: Released-label alphabets
groups.body: For each positive integer \(J\), the released-label alphabet is \(\mathcal R_J=\{1,\ldots,J\}\). In particular, \(\mathcal R_K=\{1,\ldots,K\}\) for a positive label budget \(K\); a release into \(\mathcal R_K\) may use fewer than \(K\) labels.

groups.title: Generalized quantile
groups.body:
For a probability law \(F\) with compact support in \(\mathbb R\), define
\[
Q_F(u)=\inf\{x\in\mathbb R:F((-\infty,x])\ge u\},\qquad 0<u<1.
\]
Set \(Q_F(0)=\inf\operatorname{supp}(F)\) and \(Q_F(1)=\sup\operatorname{supp}(F)\). At an atom \(x\), this convention gives \(Q_F(u)=x\) whenever \(F((-\infty,x))<u\le F((-\infty,x])\).

groups.title: Finite-measure distances
groups.body:
For finite nonnegative measures \(\mu,\nu\) on a compact interval \(S\), define their total-mass-plus-integrated-CDF distance by
\[
d_S(\mu,\nu)
=
|\mu(S)-\nu(S)|
+
\int_S
\bigl|\mu(S\cap(-\infty,t])-\nu(S\cap(-\infty,t])\bigr|\,dt.
\]
The outcome-measure distance \(d_{[0,1]}\) uses \(S=[0,1]\), with integration over \([0,1]\); the score-measure distance \(d_{\mathcal E}\) uses \(S=\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), with integration over \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).

synth_1.title: Average treatment effect functional
synth_1.body:
For any measure \(P\) on full rows \((E,Y_0,Y_1,A,Y,R)\) with score parameter \(\varepsilon\) and \(J\) labels, define the average treatment effect functional \(\theta(P)\) by
\[
\theta(P)=\int (Y_1-Y_0)\,dP.
\]

synth_4.title: Generalized quantile

Q_F(u)=\inf\{x\in\mathbb R:F((-\infty,x])\ge u\},\qquad 0<u<1.
\]
Set \(Q_F(0)=\inf\operatorname{supp}(F)\) and \(Q_F(1)=\sup\operatorname{supp}(F)\). At an atom \(x\), this convention gives \(Q_F(u)=x\) whenever \(F((-\infty,x))<u\le F((-\infty,x])\).

synth_5.title: Finite-measure distances
synth_5.body:
For finite nonnegative measures \(\mu,\nu\) on a compact interval \(S\), define their total-mass-plus-integrated-CDF distance by
\[
d_S(\mu,\nu)
=
|\mu(S)-\nu(S)|
+
\int_S
\bigl|\mu(S\cap(-\infty,t])-\nu(S\cap(-\infty,t])\bigr|\,dt.
\]
The outcome-measure distance \(d_{[0,1]}\) uses \(S=[0,1]\), with integration over \([0,1]\); the score-measure distance \(d_{\mathcal E}\) uses \(S=\mathcal E=[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), with integration over \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
